about.legalBody: 이 소프트웨어는 있는 그대로 제공되며 어떠한 보증도 없습니다. 사용 책임은 사용자에게 있으며 관할 법규를 준수하고 불법 목적으로 사용하지 마세요. AI 모델 출력의 책임은 모델 제공자에게 있으며 본 소프트웨어의 의견을 대변하지 않습니다. 기본적으로 대화·파일을 수집·업로드하지 않으며 모든 로컬 데이터는 기기에만 저장됩니다.
about.opensourceBody: 이 프로젝트는 다음 오픈 소스를 기반으로 하며 각 라이선스를 따릅니다: Electron(MIT), Chromium(BSD-3-Clause), Node.js(MIT), TypeScript(Apache-2.0), SQLite(Public Domain), better-sqlite3(MIT), pnpm(MIT). 저작권은 각 저자에게 있습니다.

checkpoints.env.changed: ⚠️ Environment changed: this rollback point recorded revision {was}, now it is {now}. Files were rolled back, but the **environment cannot be** — you may need to reinstall dependencies.
checkpoints.env.layered: Layering: file rollback relies on the rollback point itself (no container needed); environment rollback relies on the container image / snapshot.
checkpoints.env.none: No environment fingerprint on this rollback point (the project was not using a container then, or nothing was recorded)
checkpoints.env.same: Matches the current environment (files and environment line up)
checkpoints.env.title: Environment fingerprint (recorded by this rollback point)

console.empty: No events yet. New events show up here in real time.
console.hint: 이것은 **진단 이벤트 스트림**(이 기기의 이벤트 로그)이며 **콘솔이 아닙니다**. 콘솔은 컨테이너 안 셸입니다(툴바 버튼). 여기에는 실제 로컬 이벤트가 표시됩니다: 도구 호출 시작/종료, 메시 이벤트(시작/중지, 포트 바인드 실패, 피어 세션 연결/해제), 오류(미처리 + 처리됨). 최근 {n}줄만 유지하며 자격 증명으로 보이는 내용은 마스킹됩니다.

container.action.confirmStopBody: ‘{name}’을(를) 중지하고 **해당 런타임의 모든 컨테이너를 중지합니다** — 다른 프로그램이 쓰는 것 포함. 중지할까요?
container.action.needsAdmin: Starting/stopping this runtime needs administrator rights. This app will neither fail silently nor elevate for you: follow the official guide below and do it manually.
container.action.reason.install-incomple: 컨테이너 엔진 **설치가 불완전하거나 시작에 실패했습니다**(설치 항목/레지스트리 키 누락)
container.action.reason.no-exit-code: The command exited abnormally with **no exit code** (reported as-is, never treated as success)
container.action.reason.spawn-failed: The command **could not be spawned** (never started)
container.action.recovered: Recovered to an actionable state; you can retry.
container.action.timeout: Timed out: it is not ready yet (or has not stopped yet). Click "Show containers on this machine" again later.
container.action.waitingReady: Starting… (waiting until the daemon is really ready, up to about {s}s)
container.cap.none: Not ready: none of these capabilities is available
container.cardFocusHint: (you were sent here from "run/test in a container")
container.console.containerCreated: The project container was **created** (kept by default, so the writable layer survives stop/start).
container.console.intro: The console is the shell **inside the container**: its value is protection for your **host** — AI-generated commands run inside the container boundary, not on your host.
container.console.linuxNode: Images are chosen by **project tech stack**: writing/document projects are fine with a minimal image; only JS/TS/frontend projects need Linux Node inside the image (the bundled node.exe here is Windows-only).
container.console.needsImage: An in-container shell needs the project container image (the image is the container's system disk). The image source is still undecided (pulling a public image online vs shipping our own offline image), so no image is pulled and no container is started — which means no shell yet.
container.console.noExec: **No command was executed**: while the container is not ready (or the project image does not exist yet) nothing runs — and it never degrades into "running it on the host".
container.console.notEnabled: This session has not turned on "run/test in a container", so the console is unavailable.
container.console.notReady: Container not ready, so the console is unavailable (greyed out). Install or start a container in Settings → Features → Containers, then come back.
container.console.onlyInChat: The console exists only in projects and My Cattle; contacts and group chats have none.
container.console.openedInContainer: Opened a shell **inside the container**: {container} (a real `exec` into the project container, not the host shell and not the event log).
container.console.projectStopped: This project is stopped (its container is not running), so the console is unavailable. A stopped project behaves exactly like "creator offline" (existing semantics, not a new state).
container.console.security: Safety contract: **only your local manual input** ever runs; remote peers, group members, any agent, and any network content have **no injection path**; nothing runs **automatically**; secret environment variables from this machine (API keys / SMTP auth codes / identity private keys) are **never** passed into the container.
container.console.securityDetail: Contract (returned with every response, assertable): remote inject paths = {remote}; auto-run auto={auto}; secret env passed into the container secretEnv={secretEnv}.
container.console.title: Container console
container.devEnv.containerNote: This project was created with "develop in a container".
container.devEnv.note: For a project created as "in a container", starting the project always starts the container first; the choice is remembered locally.
container.devEnv.required: When you create a project you must choose: developed on this machine, or developed in a container.
container.devEnv.title: Development environment
container.devIsolation: Container = **development environment (safety isolation)**: AI-generated commands / tool calls are kept inside the boundary; it is **not meant for project testing** (testing and running are outside the container's job, so the "run/test in a container" option has been removed).
container.devIsolationTest: If we later want to run tests inside a container, that is a **separate matter**: it must be proposed on its own with its difference from "container = development environment" spelled out — **a development environment must never be quietly used as a test environment**.
container.env.install.body: Node / Python / other dependencies are **not preinstalled**, which keeps the image small and the first start fast. Install them inside the container when you need them — we only give **guidance, suggestions and links**, and never run it for you.
container.env.install.netBody: Installing packages inside the container needs network access; a faster/mirror source (apt / pip / npm) may be required. See each mirror's official docs for the exact commands — we **never run or configure it for you**.
container.env.install.noNodeForUs: Note: we never stuff Node into the image just because "the AI executor is written in Node" — the executor stays on the **host** and only the project's own commands go into the container.
container.env.install.persistBody: What you install in the container **writable layer** **survives stopping/starting the same container**, but is **lost once the container is deleted and recreated**. Do this: (1) avoid recreating that container; (2) write the install steps down (Dockerfile / script) so you can rebuild; (3) use "solidify current environment" to freeze it into a layer.
container.env.install.title: 필요할 때 개발 환경을 직접 설치하세요(의존성은 **미리 설치하지 않습니다**)
container.env.mode.body: Both the runtime and the engine's system mode are shown **as actually selected/detected**: engine mode = {mode}. Different runtimes have different modes (e.g. the Docker engine is in either Linux mode or Windows-container mode at a time), and we **never treat Linux as the default**.
container.env.mode.title: Based on your real runtime (no Linux assumption)
container.env.probe.button: Show what is inside the container
container.env.probe.refused.bad-command: That command is not in the fixed allow-list, so nothing runs (there is no "command string" parameter by design).
container.env.probe.refused.container-no: The engine is not ready, so nothing runs (start the container first).
container.env.probe.refused.no-image: No project image is available, so nothing runs.
container.env.probe.refused.project-unav: The project is unavailable: nothing runs in the container, and nothing silently falls back to running on the host.
container.env.prompt.content:
"WARMY"의 컨테이너 개발 환경을 사용하고 있습니다. 이 기기/이 컨테이너 안에서 개발 환경을 설정해 주세요.

[컨텍스트]
- 이것은 **컨테이너** 기반 개발 환경입니다. 선택된 런타임(Docker / Podman / WSL / …, 실제로 사용하는 것)을 사용합니다.
- 프로젝트 디렉터리는 컨테이너 안의 /workspace 에 마운트됩니다(우리 규칙입니다. 실제 마운트 포인트가 다르면 `pwd` / `mount` 표시를 믿으세요).
- 이 컨테이너의 배포판은 **모릅니다** — 추측으로 아무것도 설치하지 마세요.

[1단계: 먼저 탐지 후 실행]
다음을 실행하고 출력을 보여 주세요: `cat /etc/os-release`, `uname -m`, `which node python3 java go`, 존재하는 쪽의 `apt --version` / `apk --version` / `dnf --version` / `yum --version`;
그런 다음 **탐지한 실제 배포판에 따라 패키지 관리자를 선택하세요**(Debian/Ubuntu → apt; Alpine → apk; Fedora/RHEL → dnf/yum). 탐지 전에 패키지 관리자를 가정하지 마세요.

[2단계: 설명과 검증]
설치하는 모든 것에 대해 무엇인지, 버전, 경로, 검증 방법(검증 명령)을 밝히고, **전체 절차를 기록해 주세요**(환경 재구축 시 재현할 수 있도록).

[3단계: 지속성(중요)]
컨테이너 쓰기 계층에 설치된 소프트웨어는 **같은 컨테이너를 중지/시작하면 남지만, 컨테이너를 삭제하고 다시 만들면 사라집니다**. 세 가지: (1) 이 컨테이너를 재생성하지 않기; (2) 절차를 Dockerfile / 스크립트로 만들기; (3) "현재 환경 고정"(스냅샷/커밋)으로 설치된 환경을 고정하기.

[네트워크]
설치가 느리거나 실패하면 더 빠른 미러(apt / pip / npm)로 전환하는 방법과 어떤 파일이 바뀌는지 알려 주세요.

[⛔ 보안 요구]
**키 / 토큰 / 비밀번호를 컨테이너 내부 파일에 절대 쓰지 마세요**: 스냅샷/커밋은 그 시점의 전체 파일 시스템을 고정하므로 비밀이 이미지에 굽습니다. 자격 증명은 환경 변수로 주입하고 영속화하지 마세요.
container.env.prompt.failed: Copy failed (please select and copy manually)
container.env.prompt.hint: Click "Copy prompt" and paste it to an AI in your chat; it will **probe your real distribution first** and only then install.
container.env.prompt.title: Not sure how? Send this prompt to an AI in your chat
container.env.rollback.confirmBody: Rolling back **removes the current project container** and recreates it from the solidified image (an automatic solidify happens first). Note: the image only covers the container writable layer; bind-mounted project files are NOT in it - use a rollback point for files. Continue?
container.env.rollback.confirmTitle: Confirm rollback to a solidified point
container.env.rollback.done: Started a container from the solidified image: {image} (container {container})
container.env.rollback.refused.no-runtim: No container chosen yet, so there is nothing to roll back.
container.env.rollback.refused.no-solidi: There is no solidified point yet (click "Solidify current environment" first).
container.env.rollback.refused.project-u: The project is unavailable (same as the creator being offline), so the rollback is not performed.
container.env.rollback.refused.run-faile: Starting a container from the solidified image failed: the raw output is in the diagnostic event stream.
container.env.rollback.refused.runtime-c: This runtime cannot be solidified or rolled back programmatically, so we do not offer a button that is bound to fail.
container.env.solidify.ability.export-im: export/import the whole disk only (large and slow; you must do it yourself)
container.env.solidify.decision.before-d: Before a container may be destroyed ⇒ always solidify once (last chance)
container.env.solidify.decision.coalesce: Just solidified ⇒ no solidify within the throttle window
container.env.solidify.decision.explicit: You clicked "solidify current environment" ⇒ solidify once
container.env.solidify.decision.nothing-: Nothing changed in the writable layer ⇒ no need to solidify
container.env.solidify.decision.runtime-: This runtime cannot solidify ⇒ not performed
container.env.solidify.decision.throttle: Changed and past the throttle window ⇒ solidify once
container.env.solidify.executorHost: Architecture: the **AI executor stays on the host**; only the *user project's* commands/tools go into the container — so nothing needs Node in the image on our executor's behalf.
container.env.solidify.keep: Only the latest {n} solidify artifacts are kept (manually cleanable), otherwise the disk fills up.
container.env.solidify.refused.coalesced: A solidify already happened within the throttle window, so this one is skipped (one image per keystroke would be worse).
container.env.solidify.refused.commit-fa: Solidify failed (commit did not succeed): the raw output is in the diagnostic event stream, and **no** "solidified" record was written.
container.env.solidify.refused.commit-un: commit reported success but the image could not be read back, so this counts as a failure (we do not pretend it solidified).
container.env.solidify.refused.no-contai: There is no project container to solidify yet: start the project first (starting it creates the project container).
container.env.solidify.refused.no-image: Solidify did not succeed: commit did not actually succeed (no project container, engine unavailable, or the output is in the diagnostic stream) - we never write a fake "solidified" record.
container.env.solidify.refused.no-runtim: No container chosen yet: pick one from the project right-click menu first.
container.env.solidify.refused.nothing-t: There is nothing to solidify right now, so nothing is executed.
container.env.solidify.refused.runtime-c: This runtime cannot be solidified programmatically by us — follow the ability note above and do it manually.
container.env.solidify.restore: Rolling back to a solidify point belongs to the **environment** dimension and is separate from file rollback points.
container.env.solidify.retained: The project container is **kept by default** (long-lived, no --rm) ⇒ stopping/starting keeps the writable layer; that alone already gives "the next start returns to the previous state".
container.env.solidify.security: ⛔ Security notice: commit freezes the **entire filesystem at that moment** (**including potential keys / caches / temp files**). Never write secrets into container files; we **never** delete your files on our own.
container.env.solidify.throttle: Solidifying is **not "on every change"**: `docker diff` only shows how many files changed and cannot tell an installed package from cache/logs ⇒ we **throttle** (at most once per {s}s) and solidify at explicit moments (your button / before a container may be destroyed).
container.env.solidify.title: Solidify the environment (freeze it into a layer)
container.env.solidify.why.isolation-lev: It is only an isolation level, not a standalone engine
container.env.solidify.why.no-runtime-ch: No container chosen yet, so the solidify ability cannot be determined
container.env.solidify.why.oci-commit: OCI engines (Docker / Podman …) can freeze the current state into a layer
container.env.solidify.why.one-shot-vm: A one-shot sandbox VM has no persistent environment to solidify
container.env.solidify.why.runtime-unkno: The solidify ability of this runtime is unknown (stated honestly, no fake support)
container.env.solidify.why.system-servic: System containers are managed by a system service; solidifying needs elevation, which we do not run for you
container.env.solidify.why.wsl-no-commit: **WSL has no commit**: only `wsl --export/--import` of the whole disk (large and slow), which we do not run for you
container.envType.android.why: **Not a container**: docker-android style images simply run an Android emulator inside a Linux container (needs KVM; inside WSL2 it also needs nested virtualization and is finicky), or you use an emulator directly (Android SDK AVD / Genymotion / Waydroid). This app does **not** build its own Android emulator; it only explains and points you elsewhere.
container.envType.containerOnly: Only "container · Linux" really works this batch; the other four are honestly listed in the picker with "good for / prerequisites / unavailable on".
container.envType.hint: "Environment type" and "which container" are **two independent dimensions**: the same Docker engine can also be switched between Linux mode and Windows mode.
container.envType.linux.why: Mature: on Windows, Docker Desktop / Podman run Linux containers through a WSL2 or Hyper-V VM; the most free public base images exist here.
container.envType.modeHint: Note: Docker Desktop on one machine can be in **only one OS mode at a time** (Linux or Windows). Switching modes **restarts the engine**, which can take minutes — that conflicts with the idea of switching any time, so please know this before you switch.
container.envType.onlyLinux: Only Linux is implemented this round: Windows and Android are honestly labelled "limited / not a container" rather than pretended to work.
container.envType.title: Environment type
container.envType.windows: Windows (limited — not as light as a real container)
container.envType.windows.why: Limited: only nanoserver / servercore style images; **basically unavailable on Windows Home** (needs Pro/Enterprise with the container feature on); images are huge (nanoserver is about 300 MB **and has no Node in it**; servercore is about 5 GB); **Podman does not support Windows containers**.
container.fsGuard.applied: Project directory locked (one click on "Unlock directory" undoes it).
container.fsGuard.confirmBody: This adds a **deny-write** ACL on the project directory (for your own account only; reading is unaffected). It can be undone at any time and is lifted automatically when the container starts. Lock it now?
container.fsGuard.confirmLiftBody: This removes the deny-write ACL and the host side becomes writable again. Unlock now?
container.fsGuard.failed.icacls-failed: The system call failed (icacls), so nothing changed; the raw output is in the response.
container.fsGuard.failed.not-creator: Only the creator can lock or unlock this directory.
container.fsGuard.limits: 정직한 한계: 암호화도 샌드박스도 아님. 관리자나 시스템 프로세스는 여전히 쓸 수 있음.
container.fsGuard.off: Current state: not locked (the host side can write normally)
container.fsGuard.on: Current state: **locked** (the filesystem ACL is in effect; host-side writes are refused)
container.fsGuard.title: 프로젝트 디렉터리 잠금(파일시스템 수준)
container.fsGuard.unavailable.no-project: No project directory is recorded yet, so there is nothing to lock (use "Set project directory" in the project context menu first).
container.fsGuard.unavailable.not-contai: This is not a container-dev project, so there is no need to lock the host directory.
container.fsGuard.unavailable.not-creato: Only the creator can lock or unlock this directory.
container.fsGuard.unavailable.platform-n: Host directory locking is implemented on Windows only (via icacls); on other platforms we do not ship a half measure.

container.image.executorHost: Architecture: the AI executor **stays on the host**; only the *user project's* commands/tools are sent into the container (the in-container shell execs inside it). What is untrusted is the AI-generated content and the commands it wants to run — and those commands really do run inside the container. Our own executor code is trusted, so keeping it on the host does not reduce safety.
container.image.node: Images are chosen by project tech stack: plain text / document / writing projects use a minimal image (no Node); only JS / TS / frontend / Node-service projects need an image that ships Linux Node (the bundled node.exe here is Windows-only and unusable inside a container).
container.image.sourcePending: The image source (pull a public image online vs ship our own offline image) is still undecided; no image is pulled and no container is started without the product owner's consent.
container.image.stack.moreLater: Python / Go / Rust and others can be added per project need — deferred to a later batch, not piled in now.
container.image.stack.nodeOnly: **Node is needed in only two cases**: (1) the project itself is a Node stack (JS/TS/frontend/Node service); (2) the AI executor is moved into the container too. **In this product the executor stays on the host** and only the *user project's* commands/tools are sent into the container — so plain text / document / writing projects **do not** need Node: a minimal image is enough.
container.image.stack.title: Images are chosen per project tech stack
container.image.title: Image (the container's system disk)
container.image.why: An image is the container's **read-only filesystem template**; containers start from it. This app uses only **public, free, open-source** base images, pinned **by digest** (no floating tags, which could work today and change tomorrow).
container.kind.disposable-vm: Disposable sandbox VM (destroyed on close; not a long-running runtime)
container.kind.linux-vm: Linux environment (a Linux VM, not a container engine)

container.mount.body: The **entire project folder** (**including this project / chat itself**) is **bind-mounted** into the container, so changes to project files inside the container **are changes to the same files on the host** — there is no "copy the artifacts out" step. That is what makes "change it and see it right away" work.
container.mount.perf: An honest trade-off: on Windows this mount goes through WSL2, and **heavy small-file operations get noticeably slower (git repositories especially)**. That is a trade-off, not a bug; consider putting dependencies in the image or a volume.
container.mount.title: How the container sees your project (bind mount)

container.probe.startHint: Docker Desktop: starting is not a fire-and-forget click — it launches it and then **polls until the daemon is really ready** (which can take 30s to 2 minutes); only then does it become "running", and a timeout is reported honestly instead of pretending success.

container.project.blockedNotice: This project is currently unavailable ({reason}) — you can only read past records.

container.project.disableConfirmBody: Once disabled, the project is greyed out, chatting and its features are unavailable, and only past records can be read; other members see the same effect as "creator offline". Disable it?
container.project.enableNeedsContainer: To enable this project, first start a container in Settings → Features → Containers. A project cannot be enabled while its container is not running.
container.project.enforceBoundary: An honest boundary: what we can do is refuse to write or edit project files while the container is down, show the project as stopped, and disable the development entry points. What we cannot do is stop you from opening that folder in an external editor. So this is a hard application-side constraint plus a clear notice — **not** filesystem-level enforcement. (Whether to add filesystem-level measures has to be decided separately.)

container.reason.ambiguous-instances: More than one instance exists, so it is unclear which one to start/stop; no button is offered rather than risking the wrong one.
container.reason.no-podman-machine: There is no podman machine yet (run `podman machine init` first — that is an install step), so there is nothing to start.
container.reason.not-standalone-engine: It is an isolation level used together with docker / containerd, not an engine that runs containers by itself.
container.reason.one-shot-vm: It is a disposable sandbox destroyed on close, so it has no long-running state and gets no start/stop button.
container.reason.system-service-needs-ro: It is managed by a system service/daemon; starting or stopping it needs root / systemd privileges, and this app does not run elevated commands for you.
container.reason.uncertain-programmatic-: It is unclear whether this version supports programmatic start/stop; a wrong button is worse than none, so no button is offered.
container.reason.vm-not-engine: It is a Linux VM / VM manager; there is no container engine daemon on this machine to start or stop.
container.reason.vm-shutdown-affects-all: WSL is not a container engine you can start/stop on its own; `wsl --shutdown` would shut down **all** of your WSL distributions (not just this project's), so no start/stop button is offered here.

container.snapshot.body: **Under bind mounts a container snapshot does not cover project files**: commit snapshots the **container writable layer**, while the project directory is mounted from the host and lies outside it — so "a container makes project rollback easier" is **not true**.

llm.toolLimitParam: Number of cards to return (1-20, default 5)
llm.toolMaxCharsParam: Max characters returned per call (default 4000, cap 8000)
llm.toolOffsetParam: Start character offset (default 0; use it to page through long records)
llm.toolQueryParam: Search string: keywords or the user question as-is.
llm.toolRecallDesc: Search the elided conversation history by meaning/keywords. When the view shows an elision pointer ("[已省略 N 条历史 ...]") and you need a detail from it (who said what, a conclusion, a number, a path), you MUST call this instead of guessing. Args: query (string), optional limit (1-20, default 5). Returns up to `limit` cards with seq, recordId, snippet and hit source; then call retrieve on any of them for the byte-exact original.
llm.toolRecordIdParam: Record id (recordId="m-..." as shown in the pointer)
llm.toolRetrieveDesc: Fetch the byte-exact original of elided log entries by seq or recordId. Prefer the seq range and recordId samples given in the pointer. Args: recordId (string) OR seq (integer), optional offset (start char, default 0) and maxChars (per-call cap, default 4000). Returns the raw text; if it was truncated the result states the total length and the next offset so you can page through the whole record.
llm.toolSeqParam: Log sequence number (any integer inside the pointer seq range)

net.portBindFailedBody: Port {port} cannot be bound ({error}), so the mesh did not start. Your configured port was NOT changed automatically: pick an available port below, or type one yourself and retry.

net.relay.missing.needsPublicRelay: Both ends cannot connect directly — a machine with a public address is needed as a relay

net.relay.missing.unreachable: Direct connection is impossible and none of the configured relays are reachable

net.relay.unknown: Peer reachability unknown; relay need not yet determined
net.result.failPublic: Failed: not a public address (likely behind NAT / CGNAT)

net.result.pass: Passed: the address is public and outbound connectivity works
net.result.passLan: Passed (LAN mode): reachable only on the same Wi-Fi
